newsitem.title: DUBAI: HORSE RACING-DESERT STORM FORCES DUBAI WORLD CUP CANCELLATION.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DESERT STORM FORCES DUBAI WORLD CUP CANCELLATION.

text.p: A thunderstorm and flash flood on Saturday forced the cancellation of the Dubai World Cup, the world's richest horse race.
The decision was made by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum, host of the $4 million event after torrential rain at Dubai's Nad al-Sheba sand track.
Race committee spokesman Brough Scott said: "The race is off tonight."

He said Sheikh Mohammed had been walking on the race track to see what the options were and the trainers of the 13 horses entered for the race were discussing with him whether there was any way it could be held next week.
But organisers said it was unlikely the track would dry out in three or four days. Race officials said the annual event had cost about $10 million.
